written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.115: However, since power can't be extracted from the Thorium Salt, since it doesn't turn into an energy carrying liquid, you can't simply use Thorium Salt alone in any reactor design.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.116: A reactor design utilizing Thorium Salt needs to be using at least one other, additional coolants instead.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.117: The reactor core filled with Thorium Salt would house the fuel rods,  while adjacent reactor cores filled with another coolant would capture the neutrons emitted from that reactor with neutron absorber rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.118: Since the Thorium Salt main advantage is how it massively raises the maximum stat of fuel rods inside, it generally only really makes sense as a critical reactor design.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.119: Critical Thorium Salt reactors are the most efficient power generating reactors possible, but also among the hardest to build.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.12: Do not eat the nuclear fuel. Do not cook on the nuclear reactor. In case of tumors, do eat the nuclear fuel. That should be everything you need to know, now go at it and make some science!
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.121: This chapter will give you some tips and the mathematical formulas to build the most advanced and efficient reactors possible.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.122: Calculating the neutron emission¶===================¶A fuel rod will emit more neutrons onto its neighbors when it has a higher neutron count on it.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.123: The exact amount of neutrons any fuel rod would emit onto one adjacent neighbor can be calculated like this:¶¶e_n = e + ((n – s) * f)
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.124: e_n: Neutrons emitted onto neighbor¶e: Emission stat of the fuel rod¶n: Neutron count on the fuel rod¶s: Self stat of the fuel rod¶f: Factor of the fuel rod
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.125: Calculating the depletion rate of a fuel rod¶===================¶A fuel rod usually has a depletion rate of one and will therefore last as long as the time on the tooltip suggests.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.126: However, when having a greater amount neutrons on the fuel rod than the neutron maximum, the depletion rates gets multiplied by this factor:¶¶f = 4 * n / m
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.127: f: Depletion rate multiplier¶n: Neutron count on the fuel rod¶m: Maximum stat of the fuel rod
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.128: Furthermore, having the fuel rod moderated will additionally multiply its depletion rate by a factor of 4. Divide the time remaining stat of the fuel rod by the calculated depletion rate to get the real time until depletion.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.129: Tips and Tricks¶===================¶You can build reactor designs using multiple coolants. For critical reactors using moderator rods it is smarter to control one adjacent fuel rod,
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.130: rather than the moderator rod itself to control the neutron counts. Robot arms allow for precise automation of reactor cores.¶Filters can be used for easier automation of burner and breeder reactors.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.131: A higher self stat is bad in critical reactor designs, as contributes to the maximum without effecting the neutron emission.¶The emission stat is mostly irrelevant for efficiency in critical reactor designs.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.132: Setting the geiger counter sensor to hexadecimal mode is useful when trying to control neutron counts greater than 9_999. In hexadecimal mode you can compare up to 65_535 neutrons.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.14: The Nuclear Reactor Core (2x2) has slots for four reactor rods. Rods inserted into the reactor will only directly interact with directly adjacent reactor rods, also including adjacent slots on different, but adjacent, reactor core blocks.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.15: Rods can be manually inserted into a slot by right clicking it with the rod. Right clicking a slot with Pincers will pull out the reactor rod inside the slot.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.16: The reactor rods can also be automatically inserted on the top side when the reactor block is off. It is also possible to automatically extract them from the bottom side when the block is off.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.17: The reactor can be manually toggled on or off with a soft hammer. A redstone machine switch will allow controlling this with redstone. While the reactor is off, the reactor will behave as if it doesn't contain any rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.18: Individual rods can also be toggled on or off to behave as if the slot were empty. This can be done with either the redstone or manual selector.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.19: The reactor core has two internal tanks to store 64_000 liters of cold and hot coolant. Different coolant can have different effects on the inserted reactor rods. Cold coolant can be inserted from any side.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.2: First, I'll introduce you to what you'll be operating, hopefully without unplanned explosions:¶The core of any fission reactor, the 2x2 nuclear reactor core.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.20: Hot coolant will be automatically output on the red facing. If the cold coolant tank is more than half full, cold coolant will be automatically output on the blue facing. The red facing can be moved with a wrench and the blue one with a monkey wrench.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.21: While the reactor is on, Neutrons can be present on active reactor rods. The neutrons might interact with the reactor rods in different ways.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.22: Generally, the number of neutrons is directly output as HU into the reactor each tick. Neutrons only last for one second and will therefore be updated only every second.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.23: Neutron counts can be manually measured by right-clicking the reactor core with a Geiger Counter. The Geiger Counter Sensor can also be attached to the reactor core to measure the sum of all neutrons on the reactor rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.24: 100% of the percentage modes of the sensor refers to the sum of neutron maximums of all fuel rods inside the reactor core. A reactor will also emit radiation with a ranged based on the highest number of neutrons on any reactor rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.25: Building the reactor far away from any settlements and wearing a radiation hazard suit is strongly advised. Any reactor core will explode when heat gets added without coolant being present.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.26: Should new heat energy from neutrons be added when the reactor is out of coolant, the reactor will violently disintegrate.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.27: Should there be no space for the produced hot coolant remaining in the reactor, the reactor will be undergo rapid unplanned disassembly.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.29: Empty Reactor Rod¶===================¶Does nothing when inside a reactor. Doesn't accept neutrons.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.3: Some of our engineers would argue that it is just a metal box with four pistons to push the rods either in or up, that we've gone overboard with the processing power on these puppies, that four damn wires would have been sufficient.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.30: Fuel Rod¶===================¶Fuel rods emit Neutrons onto themselves and adjacent reactor rods. They have several stats that vary based on the material of the rod and the coolant that is used in the reactor.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.31: The Self stat describes how many Neutrons the rod outputs onto its own slot.¶The Emission stat describes how many Neutrons it outputs onto each adjacent reactor rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.32: The Factor stat describes how many additional neutrons it will output onto adjacent reactor rods based on how many neutrons are on itself.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.33: A bigger Factor (1/3 > 1/32) means more additional neutrons are output per neutron on the fuel rod.¶The Maximum stat describes how many neutrons can be on this fuel rod before it will be losing duration faster.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.34: When over the maximum, the fuel rod will be losing duration at minimum four times faster, scaling linearly with the amount of neutrons over the maximum.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.35: Moderated fuel rods will make adjacent active fuel rods also moderated. Moderated fuel rods will deplete four times faster and can't put neutrons onto breeder rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.36: When the remaining duration of the fuel rod runs out, it will convert to a Depleted Fuel Rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.37: Depleted Fuel Rod¶===================¶Does nothing when inside a reactor. Doesn't accept neutrons. Can be centrifuged to obtain some fuel and some higher tier fission fuel back.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.38: Absorber Rod¶===================¶Absorber rods accept neutrons from adjacent fuel rods. Each neutron on an absorber rod gets converted to two HU instead of just one.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.39: Reflector Rod¶===================¶Return any neutrons put onto them directly to their source. They therefore will never have any neutron on them.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.4: As if anyone would trust four damn wires to prevent total nuclear destruction, it is probably even not in their best interest to do so anyway. That is why in our reactor cores, every single rod controller is sentient.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.40: Moderator Rod¶===================¶Like reflector rods they return neutrons directly back to their source, but the number of neutrons they return gets multiplied by the number of fuel rods that emit neutrons onto them.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.41: They therefore can reflect up to four times as many neutrons back and will never have any neutron on them. Moderator rods also moderate adjacent fuel rods,
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.42: making them deplete four times faster and unable to put neutrons onto breeder rods. Moderated fuel rods will also make adjacent active fuel rods moderated.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.43: Breeder Rod¶===================¶Each tick, the number of neutrons on this rod get subtracted from the neutrons needed. If the needed neutrons reach zero, the rod will turn into an enriched rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.44: Breeder rods will not accept neutrons from moderated fuel rods. The loss stat gets subtracted from each number of neutrons emitted onto this rod,
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.45: meaning the loss applies to the neutrons coming from any fuel rod emitting onto it and not just once for the breeder rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.47: Distilled Water¶===================¶Converts directly into steam, doesn't need a heat exchanger. 80 HU turns 1L of Distilled Water into 160L of Steam. Moderates any fuel rods inside. No fuel rod stat changes.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.48: Semi-heavy Water¶===================¶40 HU turns 1L of Semi-heavy Water into 1L of Hot Semi-heavy Water. Moderates any fuel rods inside. No fuel rod stat changes.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.49: Heavy Water¶===================¶50 HU turns 1L of Heavy Water into 1L of Hot Heavy Water. Moderates any fuel rods inside. Divides maximum stat of fuel rods by 8.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.5: It is therefore in their best interest to not explode, as I would then get very angry at them and banish them to 'reactor rod controller'-hell!
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.50: Tritiated Water¶===================¶60 HU turns 1L of Tritiated Water into 1L of Hot Tritiated Water. Moderates any fuel rods inside. Divides maximum stat of fuel rods by 16.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.51: Industrial Coolant¶===================¶20 HU turns 1L of Industrial Coolant into 1L of Industrial Heatant. Multiplies self stat of fuel rods by 4.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.52: Multiplies emission stat of fuel rods by 4. Multiplies factor stat of fuel rods by 2.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.53: Carbon Dioxide¶===================¶20 HU turns 1L of Carbon Dioxide into 1L of Hot Carbon Dioxide. Multiplies self stat of fuel rods by 3.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.54: Helium¶===================¶30 HU turns 1L of Helium into 1L of Hot Helium. Divides emission stat of fuel rods by 2.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.55: Molten Lithium Chloride¶===================¶15 HU turns 1L of Molten Lithium Chloride into 1L of Hot Molten Lithium Chloride. Multiplies self stat of fuel rods by 5. Divides emission stat of fuel rods by 2. Increases maximum stat of fuel rods by 25%
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.56: Molten Tin¶===================¶40 HU turns 1L of Molten Tin into 1L of Hot Molten Tin. Neutrons only convert only to a third of the HU. Decreases divisor of factor stat of fuel rods by 1.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.57: Molten Sodium¶===================¶30 HU turns 1L of Molten Sodium into 1L of Hot Molten Sodium. Neutrons only convert only to a sixth of the HU. Decreases divisor of factor stat of fuel rods by 1.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.58: Molten Thorium Salt¶===================¶2_560_000 HU turns 1L of Molten Thorium Salt into 1L of Molten Lithium Chloride. Sets self stat of fuel rods to 0. Divides emission stat of fuel rods by 2. Multiplies maximum stat of fuel rods by 4.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.6: That is what we told them anyway, such a place does obviously not exist, we don't have money to fund every stupid thing. They would go to robot hell instead to be eternally incinerated and rebuild while we gather useful data.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.60: Stable nuclear fission reactors, also commonly called subcritical reactors, are a design of fission reactor that have no critical fuel rods. This means that the neutron count and thus heat output doesn't constantly increase while the reactor is running.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.61: The advantages of stable reactors are:¶- No external control required¶- Stable neutron/HU output¶- Increased Safety¶- Easy to design¶- Function with any nuclear fuel
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.62: Disadvantages of stable reactors are:¶- Not very fuel efficient¶- Only really usable as power generating reactors¶- Generally bigger than comparable critical reactors
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.63: A reactor rod can be considered critical when the number of neutrons reflected back onto the rod times the factor of the rod is greater or equal to the emission of the fuel rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.64: This means that a rod is critical if the number of reflectors around it times the factor is greater or equal to 1. So a fuel rod with a factor of 1/3 needs at least 3 adjacent reflector rods to be critical.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.65: Therefore it is advised to use Industrial Coolant as a reactor coolant for stable reactors. Industrial Coolant decreases the factor of fuel rods, making it impossible for any fuel rod to go critical without moderator rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.66: It also increases the self and emission stat which is really advantageous in stable reactors, as it means more Neutrons and therefore more efficiency.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.67: You can generally adhere to these four rules to get your stable reactor to the best efficiency:¶If the fuel used has a factor lesser than 1/8, surrounding fuel rods with absorber rods yields the greatest HU output.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.68: If the fuel used has a factor of 1/8, surrounding your fuel rods with absorber, reflector or other fuel rods yields to the exact same HU output.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.69: If the fuel used has a factor greater than 1/8, surrounding your fuel rods with reflectors or other fuel rods yields the greatest HU output.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.7: Turns out those fuckers would never insert the reactor rods at all, making the reactors perfectly safe, but also quite useless, so we overwritten their control of the rods to instead be controlled with four wires.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.70: Don't use water based coolant or moderator rods in stable reactors, as they massively decrease the duration and therefore efficiency of fuel rods by moderating them without any real benefit in stable reactor designs.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.72: Critical nuclear fission reactors, also commonly called supercritical reactors, are a design of fission reactor that have critical fuel rods. This means that the neutron count and thus heat output constantly increases while the reactor is running.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.73: The advantages of critical reactors are:¶- Greater efficiency¶- Completely configurable neutron output¶- Generally smaller than comparable stable reactors¶- Able to work as burner or breeder reactors
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.74: Disadvantages of critical reactors are:¶- Need external control¶- Constantly fluctuation HU output¶- Harder to design¶- Decreased safety¶- Need fuel with higher factors
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.75: A reactor rod can be considered critical when the number of neutrons reflected back onto the rod times the factor of the rod is greater or equal to the emission of the fuel rod.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.76: This means that a rod is critical if the number of reflectors around it times the factor is greater or equal to 1. So a fuel rod with a factor of 1/3 needs at least 3 adjacent reflector rods to be critical.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.77: Since the neutron count on the fuel rod will be indefinitely increasing, you need to control the reaction so you won't output more power than you can handle.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.78: Geiger counter sensors allow such control in an automatic fashion when combined with redstone machine switches or selectors.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.79: So when the neutron count gets too high you want to turn a reactor rod off to make the fuel rod subcritical again, making the neutron count shrink.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.8: Any rumors you might have heard of 1x1 reactor cores are just that, rumors, we would of course never build such a thing because it is obvious that the rod controller would go mad without three other ones to entertain them.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.80: For the greatest efficiency you want your neutron count on the fuel rod stay beneath the maximum stat of that fuel rod at all times, while coming as close to it as you can.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.81: You'd also want the neutron count to shrink as little as possible when controlling the reactor, so your average HU output stays as high as possible.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.82: Therefore you need a fuel with a factor of at least 1/4 to be able to build a critical reactor without the use of moderator rods.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.83: The easiest to acquire fuel that fulfills this condition is Uranium 235. You can get it by processing Uraninite. When using moderator rods the fuel can have a factor down to 1/16, so using Uranium 238 is possible.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.85: Burner Reactors are a type of nuclear fission design, with the purpose of burning through fuel rods as quickly as possible, allowing the depleted fuel rods to be processed for better nuclear fuel materials.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.86: There are two ways to make fuel rod depletion significantly quicker:¶- Moderating the fuel rod¶- Running above the neutron maximum
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.87: A fuel rod can be moderated by either by having it placed in reactor cooled with Distilled/Semi-Heavy/Heavy/Tritiated Water or placing it next to a moderator rod or moderated fuel rod. When moderated, the fuel rod will deplete four times faster.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.88: When having a neutron count greater than the maximum stat of the fuel rod on the fuel rod, it will also deplete four times faster, stacking with moderation to 16 times faster.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.89: The more you go over the maximum, the quicker the fuel rod will deplete, having a neutron count twice as high as the maximum on the rod will make it deplete twice as fast yet again, which would be stacking with moderation to 32 times faster depletion.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.9: In the unlikely case you might stumble upon such a core, which won't happen, if they existed we would have already send them to robot hell were they would reside in constant agony, which they don't because they don't exist.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.90: Neutron counts 17 times the maximum would therefore make the fuel rod deplete 17 times faster times, times 4 because of going over the maximum,
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.91: so 68 times faster, times 4 if the rod is moderated, so 272 times faster than an unmoderated rod with neutron counts below the neutron maximum.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.92: Instead of significantly increasing the neutron count on the fuel rod, it is also possible to lower the neutron maximum to take advantage of this effect.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.93: This can be easily done by using either Heavy or Tritiated Water, which lower the maximum stat by 8 and 16 times respectively and additionally also moderate all fuel rods because they are water based.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.94: To achieve really high neutron counts, it is advisable to utilize a critical reactor design, though it is also feasible to run a burner reactor as a stable design.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.95: Cobalt 60, while being almost useless as a reactor fuel itself, is really easy to burn into Thorium, which is much more useful.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.97: Breeder reactors have the goal of turning breeder rods into enriched rods. They allow getting really good nuclear fuel from lesser, more abundant fuels, like Thorium and Uranium 238.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.98: However while similar to burner reactors, they are much harder to build, requiring a non-moderated, critical reactor design. Breeder rods have a stat called loss. It describes how many neutrons are subtracted from any amount of neutrons put onto it.
written.book.Manual_Reactors.page.99: So when you have a breeder rod with a loss of 500 neutrons and try to emit 300 neutrons onto it from a single adjacent fuel rod, the breeder rod receive no neutrons, which means that the breeding process won't be advanced.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.0: This is the Manual of the Smelting Crucible and related Objects. It will explain how to use the Smelting Crucible and the Molds properly, so that you can start smelting things which cannot me molten inside a regular Furnace.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.1: If you need to know how heavy an Object is or what Materials it consists out of, just use the good old vanilla F3+H Method to enable advanced Tooltips, so you can see the most relevant Data about the Object.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.10: Step 4: Smelting¶===================¶Unless your Heat Source has some kind of Temperature regulation, you may need to shut it off once the Temperature reaches the Melting Point or else you will vaporate the Metals or worse.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.11: Step 5: Shaping¶===================¶Now just click the Side of the top of the Mold where the Crucible is next to, in order to fill it with its Metals. Warning: The Mold itself can melt too if it is made of the wrong Material.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.12: Step 5: Shaping¶===================¶Wait for the Metal to cool down, but note that you should not touch or take out the Metal while it is hot or else you will burn yourself unless you wear a Hazmat Suit or something.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.13: Mold Shapes¶===================¶The following is a List of Shapes you can chisel the Mold into. The position of the Shape on the Mold is NOT important, you can rotate and mirror it too¶X = Chiseled¶O = Not Chiseled
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.2: Step 1: Heat Source¶===================¶You need a Heat Source in order to heat up your Crucible to the desired Temperature. Possible Heat Sources may include Burning Boxes, Electric Heaters, Laser Heaters and Arc Heaters.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.3: Optional: Air Source¶===================¶In case you have to supply Air for the Crucible (for Steel), you need to point an Engine into it, which will act as a Fan. For Multiblock Crucibles the Engine has to be at the Bottom Row.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.4: Step 2: Crucible¶===================¶The choice of Crucible Material is very important. The Crucible can melt too at a certain Temperature, which is usually higher than the actual Melting Point of the Crucible itself.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.5: Step 2: Crucible¶===================¶Now place the Crucible of your choice at the Output Facing of the Heat Source. The Burning Box for example only emits to its Top Side, so you need to place the Crucible above it.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.6: Step 3: The Molds¶===================¶You probably want to cast the molten Metal into a Shape, so you need to place a Mold horizontally adjacent to the Crucible. As you may have noticed the Mold itself doesn't have a Shape.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.7: Step 3: The Molds¶===================¶This is why you need a Chisel in order to chisel the proper Shape into the Mold by using it in World. The most important Shapes are Listed in the last Pages of this Book.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.8: Step 3: The Molds¶===================¶If you somehow fail to put a correct Shape into the Mold, the End Result will be as many Nuggets as you have chiseled out places.
written.book.Manual_Smeltery.page.9: Step 4: Smelting¶===================¶Now we get to smelting. Just throw the things you want to smelt into the Crucible, or use a Hopper above the Crucible to fill it. And turn up the Heat until you reach the melting Point.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.0: This Manual is about the proper operation of a Boiler, in order to not blow yourself up. And yes there are many people who get blown up by improper operation of a Boiler.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.1: First of all you need to make sure that the Boiler you use fits the Burning Box you place below. The Tooltips will hint you the proper values you can use. The Boiler itself does accept heat from all directions, not just the Bottom.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.2: Then you need to fill the Boiler with Water on the Sides, so that you can generate Steam with it. Placing a Funnel on it and rightclicking that Funnel with a Water Bucket works for filling aswell.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.3: But if you use regular Water instead of distilled Water, then you will end up with calcification and a constant decrease of Steam-Creation-Efficiency. No risk of explosion due to that though, since it just makes less Steam per Water.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.4: Inserting Water into an empty hot Boiler, it will rapidly increase the Pressure maybe causing it to explode, depending on how much heat and water you insert at once.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.5: If a Boiler stores too much Heat without being able to convert Water into Steam, then it will simply melt and break, leaving you with a giant mess.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.6: Steam Turbines and Engines emit distilled Water to their Sides, which makes it possible to simply cycle the distilled Water back into the Boiler for having less calcification going on.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.7: The Boilers have a Barometer on their Front, their ideal State is if the Line is inside the dark green Area, so in the middle of the Barometer itself. The closer it is to the red Area, the closer it is to exploding.
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.8: Steam Engines work best if they are in green Mode, if they are too blue then they have not enough Steam (look for Boiler Calcification if it happens after a while of running normally).
written.book.Manual_Steam.page.9: If the Engines are too Red then they will release the Steam and stop running (no Explosions, just a waste of Steam and a fizzing noise).
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.0: This Manual is about common and uncommon Tools and how to use them. It contains a List of every normal Tool that you might not know the true purpose of.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.1: Swords¶===================¶It's a Sword, it deals Damage and cuts things. It can harvest Leaves, Webs and Wool Blocks.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.10: Pickaxes¶===================¶Mines Blocks like a normal Pickaxe usually does.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.11: Construction Picks¶===================¶It mines man-made Blocks much faster, but is slow on Natural Rocks.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.12: Gem tipped Pickaxes¶===================¶In an exchange for a lot of Durability, you can put flawed Gems onto your Raw Steel Pickaxe Head, to give it the Quality of a Gem Tool. Amber, Sapphires and Diamonds are best for this.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.13: JackHammers¶===================¶This thing mines Blocks and crushes them like a Hammer at an insane Speed. Not much to say about it.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.14: Mining Drills¶===================¶It can mine and shovel things at once and is the perfect universal mining Tool.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.15: Shovels¶===================¶Mines Blocks like a normal Shovel usually does.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.16: Spades¶===================¶A Spade has conditional Silk-Touch for certain Blocks, such as Dirt, Grass, Mycelium, Clay, Mud, Snow and Podzol, but it is slower than a normal Shovel and doesn't work on Sand.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.17: Plows¶===================¶The Plow harvests a 3x3x3 Area of Snow Layers and similar Blocks at once.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.18: Universal Spades¶===================¶Shovel, Saw, Sword and Crowbar at once. Very versatile, but that goes at the cost of Durability and Speed.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.19: Hammers¶===================¶Crushing Blocks and Smithery are the most common usages of this Tool. It doesn't do much else, but it can be used in Combat.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.2: Knifes¶===================¶They cut Food, Sticks, Rubber, Saplings into Sticks, Bark of a Tree, and similar things and are a somewhat usable early weapon. It can harvest all the things a Sword can harvest too.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.20: Soft Hammers¶===================¶These Hammers are mainly used to turn Machines ON and OFF. They can even turn Redstone Lamps and certain Rails ON without having to have a Redstone Signal close to them.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.21: Wrenches¶===================¶Adjusts the primary Facing of most Machines, sometimes it can be used to toggle Modes aswell.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.22: Monkey Wrenches¶===================¶Adjusts the secondary Facing of most Machines, often it can be used to toggle Modes aswell.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.23: Electric Wrenches¶===================¶They are a combination of the normal Wrench and the Monkey Wrench and can easily switch between them via Modes. Sneak Rightclick on a non-wrenchable Block to switch.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.24: Files¶===================¶Sharpens things and can comically harvest Iron Bars way faster than anything else.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.25: Chisels¶===================¶Can put Molds into Shape and change the looks of some Stones.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.26: Bending Cylinders¶===================¶Turns Plates into Curved Plates and is used for similar Metal Working procedures
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.27: Crowbars¶===================¶Opens Crates and can be used on Rails and Minecarts
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.28: Pincers¶===================¶Used to pick up hot things from Molds and Basins, so you don't have to wait for them to cool down before picking them up.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.29: Plungers¶===================¶Empties Pipes and Fluid Tanks by either voiding the Fluid or dropping the ItemStack that is stuck in them. Works on Thaumic Conduits aswell.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.3: Butchery Knifes¶===================¶Has a Looting Modifier on it per Default, but has a slow swing and low Damage.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.30: Scoops¶===================¶Catches Butterflies, Bees and Bumblebees, also needed to harvest Bumble Hives and Bee Hives.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.31: Hoes¶===================¶They till the ground, what do you expect? I'm not gonna explain vanilla Tools in great detail.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.32: Branch Cutters¶Trimmers¶===================¶Cuts Saplings out of Leaves with high precision, like a Grafter.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.33: Senses¶===================¶Harvests a 3x3x3 Area of Crops, Flowers and Tall Grass.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.34: Rolling Pins¶===================¶Flattens Dough and Clay for cooking and crafting purposes.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.35: Scissors¶===================¶Can cut Tripwires on Rightclick, shear Sheep and harvest Wool-ish/Cloth-ish Blocks.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.36: Screwdrivers¶===================¶Drives Screws and such. The most common usage is adjusting Modes on Blocks and Covers. They can rotate Comparators and Repeaters.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.37: Wire Cutters¶===================¶They harvest Wires. Another usage is to adjust Wires and in some cases Covers aswell.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.38: Hand Mixers¶===================¶These are just so you don't consume your Hunger Bar when operating the Mixing Bowl.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.39: Hand Drills¶===================¶Those Drill Holes in Surfaces. If you have Dynamite Sticks or Iron/Steel Rods with you, you can stick the Dynamite into Walls or reinforce Bricks and Concrete.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.4: Clubs¶===================¶Sometimes kindof expensive, but it works like a Hammer and deals lots of Damage, while having a larger cooldown time after a hit. It can break Rocky Blocks, but it will crush them.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.40: Flint and Tinder¶===================¶Sets things on Fire and can light anything that requires ignition. But it might take a few tries to do so.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.41: Magnifying Glasses¶===================¶With this you can look at the Details of a LOT of things in GregTech, just put a Lens of any kind on a Stick and you are good to go for a long time.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.42: Pocket Multitool¶===================¶A Multi-Tool that can be switched to the most common purposes. See it as a Swiss Army Knife.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.5: Axes¶===================¶Good in chopping down Trees, bad in chopping down Planks or other wooden things.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.6: Double Axes¶===================¶Still good for chopping on Trees, but also very effective as a Weapon and has 50% more Durability than the normal Axe, while requiring 66.666% more Material to create.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.7: Saws¶===================¶Bad for chopping Trees, but can easily cut wooden things like Planks.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.8: Chainsaws¶===================¶Good for pretty much all purposes, can chop Trees, saw Planks and is a very nice Weapon. It can specifically be used to spam click Creepers to death easily.
written.book.Manual_Tools.page.9: Buzzsaws¶===================¶This Type of Saw is dedicated to Hand Crafting and cannot harvest any Blocks. It is cheaper to use this than a Chainsaw for crafting purposes.
